title: Safe and Orderly Restoration of Singapore's Air Connectivity
what_it_is: Safe and Orderly Restoration of Singapore's Air Connectivity

sections.label: Border reopening and travel frameworks
sections.summary: MOT and CAAS worked with MOH on a calibrated border reopening, launching about 30 VTLs from September 2021 and the VTF in April 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Over the past one and a half years, the Ministry of Transport (MOT) and the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) have worked closely with the Ministry of Health (MOH) on a cautious and calibrated approach to reopening our borders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We commenced and progressively launched, as Members would recall, about 30 Vaccinated Travel Lanes (VTLs) over a period of six months, from September 2021, with a comprehensive set of safeguards, including vaccination and testing requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: With the experience gained from these VTLs, we established the Vaccinated Travel Framework (VTF) in April 2022, which removed quarantine and testing requirements for all fully vaccinated travellers.

sections.label: Worker vaccination protection levels
sections.summary: Almost 100% of workers have attained minimum protection as defined by MOH, and about half have up-to-date protection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As of now, almost 100% of the workers have attained minimum protection as defined by MOH and about half have up-to-date protection.

sections.label: Changi Airport passenger traffic recovery
sections.summary: Average weekly passenger traffic at Changi Airport has recovered to about 80% of pre-COVID-19 levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To date, average weekly passenger traffic at Changi Airport has recovered to about 80% of pre-COVID-19 levels.

sections.label: China-Singapore weekly flights
sections.summary: There are currently 38 weekly flights between China and Singapore, including two recently approved flights to Beijing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: At present, there are 38 weekly flights between China and Singapore, which includes two recently approved flights to Beijing.

sections.label: Travellers from China residency status
sections.summary: More than 60% of these travellers from China are Singapore Citizens, Permanent Residents and Long-Term Pass Holders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: More than 60% of these travellers from China are Singapore Citizens (SC), Permanent Residents (PRs) and Long-Term Pass Holders (LTPH).

sections.label: Up-to-date vaccination rates
sections.summary: The up-to-date rate is about 60% for the whole population and 67% to closer to 70% for those aged 80 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The up-to-date rate is not bad at all.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It is about 60% for the whole population.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Amongst those aged 80 and above, it is actually 67% to closer to 70%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As I mentioned just now, bivalent vaccination is happening at about 13,000 doses per day, which is a very healthy volume.

sections.label: Singapore vaccination status definition
sections.summary: MOH requires minimum protection of three mRNA or four Sinovac shots, plus an additional shot five to 12 months later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But the Member is right that, in Singapore, as Members are aware, MOH has revised our vaccination status definition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We require minimum protection, which is three shots for mRNA, or four shots for Sinovac.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And after that, we require another additional shot five to 12 months after the previous shot to keep yourself up to date.

sections.label: WHO definition for travellers
sections.summary: Aligning vaccination definitions for residents and all travellers is impractical, so the less strict WHO definition is used for travellers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It is not practical to fully align the vaccination definition for people living here and for travellers from all around the world, because every country has their own definition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And that is why we use the WHO definition, which is less strict on travellers from all sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Omicron alone, there are about 650 Omicron sub-variants.

sections.label: PDT not foolproof
sections.summary: PDT is not foolproof because a person can test negative while incubating and become positive on the plane or upon arrival.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The second point to note is that PDT is not foolproof.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Because, first, you can be incubating and when you test before you board the plane, you are negative, but on the plane or upon arrival, you develop disease and you become positive.

sections.label: Protocols buy time
sections.summary: PDT, OAT, SHN or combinations can buy time, as when Omicron was first detected coming from Africa.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Third point is that certain protocol that the Member mentioned: PDT, OAT, SHN or combination, can buy us time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Let us say we detect something that sounds serious, which you can recall, when we first detected Omicron coming from Africa, we have to implement a combination of those measures.

sections.label: mRNA platform importance
sections.summary: With mRNA technology, development can hopefully happen in 100 days, making the mRNA platform important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: With mRNA technology, hopefully, that can happen in 100 days and that is why it is important to go onto the mRNA platform.

sections.label: Air connectivity with China
sections.summary: Flights and passenger volumes between China and Singapore are 10% or less of pre-COVID-19 levels, leaving significant scope to restore air connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As I have stated earlier in my reply, whether you look at it in terms of flights or in terms of passenger volumes, we are well below where we were, in fact, 10% – or less – compared to pre-COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, there is clearly significant scope to restore air connectivity and the passenger flows between China and Singapore.

sections.label: Restoring China air connectivity
sections.summary: Changi Airport must manage increases safely, but Singapore wants to restore air connectivity with China and welcomes China's announcements, though a near-term surge is unlikely.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We also need to take into account Changi Airport's own ability to manage any increases, and to do so in a manner that ensures safe and smooth travel for passengers.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But we are quite clear that directionally, this is what we want to do as we have with the rest of the world, we want to restore air connectivity with China, and we welcome the latest announcements and moves by China.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But in the near term, if you ask me, will there be a surge?

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I think unlikely, but neither will we be at a standstill.

sections.label: SG Arrival Card contact tracing
sections.summary: The SG Arrival Card may add questions targeting MERS, Ebola and Mpox, letting authorities trace a traveller's flight and close contacts if disease is detected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Maybe we will review to see whether we can add a few more questions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But the purpose is, it is not targeted at COVID-19 but targeted at Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS), at Ebola, Mpox and so on, that can arise and can infect travellers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: While travellers declare whether they feel well or unwell, the fact is they leave behind a contact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, if someone falls sick, goes to a doctor and we detect is MERS, for example – we are always on the lookout for MERS – we know which flight the person came off, who are their close contacts and if we want to do contact tracing, we can do so through the SG Arrival Card mechanism.

sections.label: Hospital capacity and transitional care
sections.summary: COVID-19 inpatients are low but non-ICU ward utilisation is high due to ageing, so step-down Transitional Care Facilities are being set up while Woodlands Healthcare campus is delayed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, the number of COVID-19 inpatients is actually low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, it is not actually burdening our hospital system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: However, the hospital system utilisation of non-ICU wards is high because we are ageing – more people are falling sick.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Woodlands Healthcare campus, for example, was delayed for two to three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We hope it can start opening by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: You cannot rush the building of a hospital, but what we can do, which I have announced and explained in this House before, is to set up step-down facilities, particularly Transitional Care Facilities (TCF) that proved to be very helpful.
